rubric_items.reason: CO-1..CO-7 and EP-1 are all in the code. Two small gaps: the links drop page instead of setting page=1, and the status_counts response type is inlined in client.ts, not added to web/src/api/types.ts as CO-5 says.
SQL is in the repo and the rule is in the service, with strict types. The only break from the list shape is the one the user decided (A-03), and the design records it.
Six files changed, all named by design components. The router is untouched. The listWhere extraction is the shared builder the design asks for.
Input validation is unchanged. Statuses with no rows are filled with 0. Count query errors reach the existing asyncHandler. The web view renders only when data is present.
The summary matches the diff. One statement is not backed: it says the design asks for no regression test, but the design says nothing about tests. One claim also cites the wrong line.

findings.text: CO-7 says each count links with page=1. The code deletes the page param instead. That likely behaves the same if a missing page defaults to 1, but it is not the literal design.

cites.quote: Each one links to the current query string with `status=<STATUS>` and `page=1`.

findings.suggested_fix: Either set page=1 explicitly or note in the design/summary that an absent page means page 1.

findings.text: CO-5 puts status_counts on the appointments list response type in web/src/api/types.ts. The code adds only AppointmentStatusCounts there and inlines the intersection type in client.ts.

cites.quote: plus `status_counts` on the appointments list response type

findings.suggested_fix: Add a named list response type in web/src/api/types.ts and use it in client.ts, or update the summary.

findings.text: The summary says the design asks for no regression test. The design says nothing about tests either way, so this reason is not backed by the input.

cites.quote: Tests: none added. The design asks for no regression test

findings.suggested_fix: Say the design does not mention tests and they are left to the unit-test step.
